umbrella.reason: The kernel lifting and image intersection equivalences are proved by actual element lifts. The subgroup product in UA.Q is a set product; no unproved permutability is used.

The induction on support inclusion isolates pure kernel factors inside the subgroup generated by the marked tuples. It proves equality with the full compatible product, the precise kernel of every marked subgroup, and IP using base IP. Local recognition explicitly needs an antichain. The lower-central argument repeats the same isolation inside the lower-central subgroup. The separator proof uses normality to reorder factors. The two-factor split description and actual generation in UA.Fiber are proved, not inferred from orders.

Normality places each cross-commutator in two different factors; independent coordinates make it trivial. The actual multiplication map is injective by coordinate detection. Exact equality of the base kernel with the join is needed for the full product conclusion; containment suffices only for injectivity. The presentation adapter checks local embeddings, their normal images and the complete residual base presentation. This is the already independently reviewed normal-kernel argument, now integrated into the applications.

Boolean deletions commute on the markers. The map into the compatible product has exactly their common kernel. UA.Fiber proves that its images generate the whole target. This proof is correct without any finite-order comparison. A later commuting-retraction supplement is not silently substituted into this frozen edition.

IP alone is not treated as geometric recognition. Pairwise cosets are moved into the same base fiber using the actual marked intersection subgroup and base IP. Coordinate subgroups then give a common representative. Thinness, connectivity of residues, and freeness of the full type-preserving chamber action are separately proved. Local involutivity is explicit, including a counterexample if it is omitted.

Burnside gives the original independent degree-one coordinates. A purported edge relation in degree two is separated at a deepest participating forest edge. The graded Lie argument and the descending finite nilpotent factorization then force that original edge commutator to vanish, using IP in the original group. No intersection property of an intermediate quotient is assumed. The resulting class-two coordinate model has a complete collected presentation.

The finite nilpotent universal quotient has explicit finite graded bounds. Retractions identify the lower-central subgroup of each marked subgroup. The target order bounds the number of strict lower-central descents. The all-subset kernel condition is exactly the quotient IP condition. The invariant hyperplane argument supplies the exhaustive normal-subgroup ladder. The generator-permutation equivalence is specified, rather than replaced by abstract isomorphism.

The affine normal form proves the full presentation, and the two invariant lattices give exact orders and relators. Deletion stability is checked on those relators. The two doubled translations may coincide in H6; neither the kernel formula nor the recognition argument assumes their cyclic factors are independent. The square and diagonal semidirect decompositions follow from actual affine subgroups, including q=1.

The order bound n>=5 follows from two order-eight local groups intersecting in order two. Burnside and irredundance give a character that agrees with orientation parity on every affine reflection, so the presentation kernel preserves orientation. A finite-order plane isometry has a fixed point; the square tiling moves it into a fundamental triangle, whose stabilizers are conjugates of proper local parabolics. Exact pair orders make the quotient injective on those stabilizers, excluding kernel torsion. An orientation-preserving affine element with nontrivial finite linear part is a finite-order rotation, so the kernel consists of translations. Its invariant lattice is an ideal of Z[i]; the norm is a power of two, hence the ideal is a power of (1+i). This gives exactly the two displayed lattices. The elementary plane stabilizers and Gaussian Euclidean/UFD facts remain explicit classical inputs.

Dihedral attachments have faithful proper marked subgroups; the even-label restriction and unselected-pair argument are explicit. The amalgam discussion retains injective factors and reduced normal forms, then proves its universal property, torsion inheritance, infinitude under properness on both sides, and finite generation. The simultaneous compatible product is not confused with a pushout.
